category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: Which Risk Group (RG) and transmission routes define BSL-2 containment?
back:
- Risk Group 2 (RG-2).
- Transmission via ingestion, percutaneous injury, or mucous membrane exposure.
citation: BSL-2 | RG-2: Agents that pose moderate hazards to personnel and the environment. Transmission via ingestion, percutaneous, or mucous membrane.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: Why are Biosafety Cabinets (BSC) required for centrifugation or vortexing in BSL-2?
back:
- To prevent exposure to aerosols.
- Uses Class I or II BSCs to contain infectious droplets generated during these procedures.
citation: Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) used for aerosol-generating procedures (centrifugation, vortexing).

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: Contrast the access and signage requirements of BSL-2 labs versus BSL-1.
back:
- BSL-2: Restricted lab access and mandatory biohazard warning signs.
- BSL-1: Open benchwork with standard practices and no specific access restriction.
citation: BSL-2: Restricted lab access; biohazard warning signs... BSL-1: Standard microbiological practices; open benchwork.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: A technician handles Staphylococcus aureus on an open bench. What BSL-2 facility feature is missing?
back:
- Biosafety Cabinet (BSC) for potential aerosols.
- Autoclave for waste decontamination must be available on-site.
citation: Staphylococcus aureus... Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) used for aerosol-generating procedures... autoclave available for waste.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: What is the specific post-exposure step for a needle-stick injury involving BSL-2 HIV samples?
back:
- Start 3-drug ART (HIV PEP) within 2-72 hours.
- Duration: 28 days.
citation: HIV PEP: Start 3-drug antiretroviral therapy (ART) within 2 to 72 hours for 28 days.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: List three bacterial and two viral pathogens handled under BSL-2 protocols.
back:
- Bacteria: Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella spp., Vibrio cholerae.
- Viruses: Hepatitis B (HBV), Hepatitis C (HCV), or HIV.
citation: Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella spp., Hepatitis B & C viruses, HIV, Vibrio cholerae.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: How is BSL-2 laboratory waste managed to prevent environmental contamination?
back:
- Segregate at source into color-coded bins.
- Use Yellow Bags for infectious waste; autoclave before final disposal.
citation: Infectious & Anatomical Waste... Yellow Bag... autoclave available for waste.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: Differentiate BSL-2 from BSL-3 based on primary transmission route and air pressure requirements.
back:
- BSL-2: Ingestion/Percutaneous; no mandatory negative pressure.
- BSL-3: Inhalation (aerosol); requires controlled negative air pressure and HEPA filtration.
citation: BSL-2: Transmission via ingestion, percutaneous... BSL-3: lethal disease through inhalation/aerosol route. Controlled negative air pressure.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Which specific high-risk pathogens are handled in BSL-3 laboratories?
back:
• Mycobacterium tuberculosis
• Brucella spp.
• Bacillus anthracis
• SARS-CoV-2
citation: BSL-3 Bio-Risk Organisms: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Brucella spp., Bacillus anthracis, SARS-CoV-2.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: What is the critical airflow requirement for BSL-3 containment labs?
back:
• Controlled negative air pressure
• Directional airflow (pulling air into the lab)
• Continuous airflow monitoring
citation: BSL-3 Safety Protocols: Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); continuous airflow monitoring.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: How does BSL-3 exhaust air treatment differ from lower levels?
back:
• Exhaust air must undergo HEPA filtration
• Prevents release of aerosolized pathogens into the environment
citation: BSL-3 Safety Protocols: HEPA filtration of exhaust air.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: A lab processes sputum for Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Describe the mandatory facility and PPE requirements.
back:
• Facility: BSL-3 with negative pressure
• PPE: N95/FFP2 respirator, gown, gloves, and eye protection
citation: BSL-3: Mycobacterium tuberculosis... Controlled negative air pressure; N95 / FFP2 respirator, gown, gloves, and eye protection.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Which Biosafety Cabinet (BSC) classes are mandatory for BSL-3 procedures?
back:
• BSC Class II
• BSC Class III
• Used for all aerosol-generating manipulations
citation: BSL-3 Safety Protocols: BSC Class II or III.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Identify the WHO Risk Group (RG) designation for BSL-3 agents.
back:
• Risk Group 3 (RG-3)
• Indigenous or exotic agents causing serious/lethal disease via inhalation
citation: BSL-3 Risk Group: RG-3: Indigenous or exotic agents that may cause serious or potentially lethal disease through inhalation/aerosol route.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Describe the required entry/exit configuration for a BSL-3 laboratory.
back:
• Double-door entry airlock
• Separates the lab from general access corridors
citation: BSL-3 Safety Protocols: double-door entry airlock.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Compare aerosol management in BSL-2 versus BSL-3 facilities.
back:
• BSL-2: BSC used only for aerosol-generating procedures
• BSL-3: All infectious work must occur within a BSC with negative room pressure
citation: BSL-2: BSC Class I or II used for aerosol-generating procedures; BSL-3: Controlled negative air pressure... BSC Class II or III.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: What specific hand hygiene facility is required for BSL-3?
back:
• Hands-free sink
• Typically foot-pedal or sensor-operated
• Located near the exit door
citation: BSL-3 Safety Protocols: hands-free sink.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: What is the primary route of transmission for BSL-3 bio-risk organisms?
back:
• Inhalation route
• Aerosol transmission
citation: BSL-3 Risk Group: agents that may cause serious or potentially lethal disease through inhalation/aerosol route.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: What level of risk and hazard do BSL-2 agents pose to laboratory personnel?
back: BSL-2 agents correspond to Risk Group 2 (RG-2), posing moderate hazards to personnel and the environment.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [BSL-2] RG-2: Agents that pose moderate hazards to personnel and the environment.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: What are the three primary routes of transmission for pathogens handled in BSL-2 labs?
back: Transmission occurs via: 1. Ingestion 2. Percutaneous (needle-sticks) 3. Mucous membrane exposure.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: Transmission via ingestion, percutaneous, or mucous membrane.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Which facility feature distinguishes BSL-2 lab access from BSL-1?
back: BSL-2 requires restricted lab access and the display of biohazard warning signs, unlike the open access of BSL-1.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: Restricted lab access; biohazard warning signs.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: A lab technician must vortex a Salmonella sample; which primary containment device is required?
back: A Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) is mandatory for aerosol-generating procedures like vortexing or centrifugation.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) used for aerosol-generating procedures (centrifugation, vortexing).

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: What is the mandatory method for decontaminating BSL-2 biological waste before disposal?
back: An autoclave must be available and used for the decontamination of infectious laboratory waste.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: autoclave available for waste.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Which universal symbol must be posted at the entrance of a BSL-2 facility?
back: The Biohazard warning sign.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: biohazard warning signs.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: How does BSL-2 air handling differ from BSL-3 requirements?
back: BSL-2 does not require negative air pressure or HEPA-filtered exhaust, which are mandatory for BSL-3.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [BSL-3] Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); HEPA filtration of exhaust air.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: A sample contains Bloodborne pathogens (HBV/HIV); which biosafety level is appropriate for diagnostic work?
back: BSL-2 is required for handling Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [BSL-2 Bio-Risk Organisms] Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella spp., Hepatitis B & C viruses, HIV.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: What is the daily protocol for maintaining work surface safety in BSL-2?
back: Daily decontamination of work surfaces with appropriate disinfectants (e.g., 10% sodium hypochlorite).
citation: Patient safety ID.md: decontamination of work surfaces daily.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: What are the essential PPE components for routine work in BSL-2?
back: Standard PPE includes lab coats and gloves; eye protection is added if splashes are anticipated.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: personal protective equipment (lab coat, gloves as needed).

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: What is the primary transmission route for pathogens necessitating BSL-3 containment protocols?
back: Inhalation or aerosol route. BSL-3 handles indigenous or exotic agents that cause serious or potentially lethal disease.
citation: BSL-3: RG-3: Indigenous or exotic agents that may cause serious or potentially lethal disease through inhalation/aerosol route.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Describe the directional airflow requirement essential for maintaining BSL-3 facility safety.
back: Controlled negative air pressure. Air must flow from clean areas into the laboratory to prevent pathogen escape.
citation: BSL-3: Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); continuous airflow monitoring.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: How does the entrance design of BSL-3 labs contrast with standard BSL-2 facilities?
back: BSL-3 requires a double-door entry airlock. BSL-2 only requires restricted access and biohazard warning signs.
citation: BSL-3: double-door entry airlock... BSL-2: Restricted lab access; biohazard warning signs.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: A lab processes Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Which exhaust protocol prevents environmental release of this agent?
back: HEPA filtration of exhaust air. This ensures all air leaving the BSL-3 facility is sterile.
citation: BSL-3: HEPA filtration of exhaust air; continuous airflow monitoring.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Which specific types of Biosafety Cabinets (BSC) are mandatory for BSL-3 laboratory procedures?
back: BSC Class II or Class III. These cabinets provide the necessary barrier for aerosol-generating procedures.
citation: BSL-3: BSC Class II or III; used for inhalation/aerosol route agents.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: List four high-risk organisms that must be handled strictly under BSL-3 conditions.
back: 1. Mycobacterium tuberculosis 2. Brucella spp. 3. Bacillus anthracis 4. SARS-CoV-2
citation: Bio-Risk Organisms (BSL-3): Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Brucella spp., Bacillus anthracis, SARS-CoV-2.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: What hands-on facility feature is required in BSL-3 to prevent contact cross-contamination?
back: Hands-free sink. This allows personnel to perform hand hygiene without touching potentially contaminated faucet handles.
citation: BSL-3: hands-free sink; personal protective equipment (gown, gloves, N95).

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Distinguish the respiratory protection used in BSL-3 from the suit requirements of BSL-4.
back: BSL-3: Fitted N95/FFP2 respirators. BSL-4: Positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-boxes.
citation: BSL-3: fitted N95 / FFP2 respirator... BSL-4: positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: Q: Which specific categories of organisms are typically handled in a BSL-1 laboratory?
back:
- Well-characterized agents
- Not known to cause disease in immunocompetent humans
- Examples: E. coli K-12, Bacillus subtilis, Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-1: Well-characterized agents not known to consistently cause disease in immunocompetent adult humans. E. coli (K-12 strains), Bacillus subtilis, Saccharomyces cerevisiae.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: Q: What is the primary pathophysiological assumption regarding BSL-1 agents and adult health?
back: These agents do not consistently cause disease in healthy, immunocompetent adults and are considered low individual and community risk (Risk Group 1).
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [RG-1: Well-characterized agents not known to consistently cause disease in immunocompetent adult humans.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: Q: How does the benchwork protocol in BSL-1 differ from higher biosafety levels?
back:
- BSL-1 utilizes open benchwork.
- Higher levels (BSL-2+) require Biosafety Cabinets (BSC) or restricted access for aerosol-generating procedures.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-1: Standard microbiological practices; open benchwork... BSL-2: Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) used for aerosol-generating procedures.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: Q: Why must a student with advanced HIV infection take extra precautions in a BSL-1 lab?
back: BSL-1 protocols are designed for *immunocompetent* adults. Immunocompromised individuals are at risk of opportunistic infection from otherwise non-pathogenic agents.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [RG-1: Well-characterized agents not known to consistently cause disease in immunocompetent adult humans.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: Q: What is the mandatory maintenance requirement for laboratory work surfaces in BSL-1?
back: Surfaces must be decontaminated daily and immediately following any spill of viable biological material.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-1: decontamination of work surfaces daily.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: Q: List the four essential facility and equipment components of a standard BSL-1 lab.
back:
1. Handwashing sink
2. Open benchwork
3. Standard personal protective equipment (Lab coats/gloves)
4. Daily surface decontamination
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-1: Standard microbiological practices; open benchwork; handwashing sink; personal protective equipment (lab coat, gloves as needed); decontamination of work surfaces daily.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: Q: Under what specific conditions are gloves mandated as PPE in a BSL-1 setting?
back: Gloves are utilized 'as needed' based on risk assessment (e.g., handling concentrated cultures, hazardous chemicals, or if the worker has non-intact skin).
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-1: personal protective equipment (lab coat, gloves as needed)]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: Q: Differentiate between the disposal of BSL-1 microflora cultures vs. non-contaminated office paper.
back:
- Cultures: Disinfected/Autoclaved then Yellow Bag.
- Office Paper: General Non-Infectious Waste (Black/Green Bin) for municipal landfill.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [General Non-Infectious Waste: Office paper, packaging... Black / Green Bin... Sent directly to municipal landfill disposal.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: Which type of biological agents are handled in Biosafety Level 3 (BSL-3) laboratories?
back:
* Indigenous or exotic agents.
* Pathogens causing serious/lethal disease.
* Transmission via inhalation/aerosol route.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-3 RG-3: Indigenous or exotic agents that may cause serious or potentially lethal disease through inhalation/aerosol route.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: What is the mandatory airflow requirement for a BSL-3 facility to ensure containment?
back:
* Controlled negative air pressure.
* Directional airflow into the laboratory.
* Continuous airflow monitoring.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); continuous airflow monitoring.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: How is exhaust air handled in a BSL-3 laboratory before environmental release?
back:
* HEPA (High-Efficiency Particulate Air) filtration.
* Required for all exhaust air to prevent aerosol release.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [HEPA filtration of exhaust air; double-door entry airlock.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: Following a biological spill in BSL-3, what is the first critical action regarding aerosols?
back:
* Evacuate the room immediately.
* Notify all personnel.
* Wait 30 minutes for aerosols to settle before re-entry.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [If an aerosol is generated, evacuate the room immediately and wait 30 minutes for aerosols to settle before re-entering.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: What is the preferred disinfectant and contact time for decontaminating a BSL-3 spill?
back:
* Disinfectant: 10% Sodium Hypochlorite (freshly prepared).
* Contact Time: 20 to 30 minutes.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Apply Disinfectant: Pour a freshly prepared disinfectant (10% Sodium Hypochlorite... Allow an undisturbed contact time of 20 to 30 minutes.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: List four high-risk pathogens typically requiring BSL-3 containment protocols.
back:
* Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
* Bacillus anthracis.
* Brucella spp.
* SARS-CoV-2.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [Bio-Risk Organisms: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Brucella spp., Bacillus anthracis, SARS-CoV-2.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: What respiratory protection is mandatory for personnel working within BSL-3 containment?
back:
* Fitted N95 or FFP2 respirator.
* Used to prevent inhalation of infectious aerosols.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Airborne Precautions: Fitted N95 / FFP2 respirator, gown, gloves, and eye protection inside negative-pressure isolation rooms.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: Contrast the entry protocols between BSL-2 and BSL-3 laboratory facilities.
back:
* BSL-2: Restricted access with biohazard signs.
* BSL-3: Double-door entry airlock mandatory.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-2: Restricted lab access; biohazard warning signs. BSL-3: double-door entry airlock; hands-free sink.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: Where must aerosol-generating procedures (e.g., vortexing) be performed in a BSL-3 lab?
back:
* Biosafety Cabinet (BSC).
* Specifically Class II or Class III BSC.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-3... BSC Class II or III; continuous airflow monitoring.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: What type of sink is required in BSL-3 to prevent contact contamination?
back:
* Hands-free sink.
* Located near the exit of the laboratory.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-3... double-door entry airlock; hands-free sink; BSC Class II or III.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Which specific high-risk viral agents are strictly handled in a Biosafety Level 4 (BSL-4) facility?
back:
Dangerous and exotic agents including:
- Ebola virus
- Marburg virus
- Lassa virus
- Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus.
citation: BSL-4 Table: Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: What are the two primary containment methods for protecting personnel in BSL-4 laboratories?
back:
1. Positive-pressure air-fed suits.
2. Class III glove-box Biosafety Cabinets (BSC).
citation: BSL-4 Table: Positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Contrast the exhaust air filtration requirements between BSL-3 and BSL-4 facilities.
back:
- BSL-3: Single HEPA filtration of exhaust air.
- BSL-4: Dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust filtration.
citation: BSL-4 Table: dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust; [BSL-3] HEPA filtration of exhaust air.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: A researcher is exiting a BSL-4 containment zone. What mandatory decontamination step must be completed?
back: The researcher must pass through a full chemical decontamination shower exit to neutralize any pathogens on the exterior of the suit.
citation: BSL-4 Table: full chemical decontamination shower exit.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: How is the air supply managed in a BSL-4 facility to prevent environmental contamination?
back: The facility uses a dedicated air supply system combined with double-HEPA filtration for all exhaust air to ensure no pathogens are released.
citation: BSL-4 Table: dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Define the Risk Group (RG) criteria for organisms that mandate BSL-4 containment.
back: Risk Group 4 (RG-4): Dangerous/exotic agents with high individual and community risk, typically aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening, and lacking vaccines or treatments.
citation: BSL-4 Table: RG-4: Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk of aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections with no vaccines/treatments.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: What is the structural requirement for the location of a BSL-4 laboratory?
back: The laboratory must be housed in a strictly isolated building or a completely segregated zone within a building.
citation: BSL-4 Table: Isolated building/zone.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Why is CCHF virus handled in BSL-4 while SARS-CoV-2 is handled in BSL-3?
back: CCHF poses a higher community risk with high mortality and lacks widespread treatment/vaccines, whereas BSL-3 manages indigenous/exotic agents like SARS-CoV-2 which have established management protocols.
citation: BSL-3 Table: Indigenous or exotic agents... SARS-CoV-2. BSL-4 Table: High individual and community risk... no vaccines/treatments.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Explain the role of the Class III Biosafety Cabinet in BSL-4 operations.
back: It acts as a gas-tight, physical barrier (glove-box) allowing safe handling of lethal agents without the need for positive-pressure suits.
citation: BSL-4 Table: Class III glove-box BSC.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Which Biosafety Level is required for agents that pose high individual and community risk?
back: Biosafety Level 4 (BSL-4).
citation: BSL-4 Table: RG-4: Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: What is the defining risk level and hazard profile for Biosafety Level 2 (BSL-2)?
back: BSL-2 handles Risk Group 2 (RG-2) agents. These pose moderate hazards to personnel and the environment if accidentally released.
citation: RG-2: Agents that pose moderate hazards to personnel and the environment.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: What are the three primary routes of transmission for agents handled in a BSL-2 facility?
back:
1. Ingestion
2. Percutaneous (needle-sticks)
3. Mucous membrane exposure.
citation: Transmission via ingestion, percutaneous, or mucous membrane.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: Which specific bloodborne viral pathogens are managed under BSL-2 containment protocols?
back: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV), Hepatitis C Virus (HCV), and Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV).
citation: Hepatitis B & C viruses, HIV, Vibrio cholerae.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: What equipment is mandatory for aerosol-generating procedures like centrifugation in BSL-2?
back: A Biosafety Cabinet (BSC), specifically Class I or Class II, must be utilized for such procedures.
citation: Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) used for aerosol-generating procedures (centrifugation, vortexing).

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: What is the required concentration and contact time for Sodium Hypochlorite in spill management?
back: A freshly prepared 10% solution must be applied for 20 to 30 minutes to ensure microbial inactivation.
citation: Apply Disinfectant: Pour a freshly prepared disinfectant (10% Sodium Hypochlorite... Allow an undisturbed contact time of 20 to 30 minutes.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: What administrative and facility access controls are required for a BSL-2 laboratory?
back:
1. Restricted laboratory access
2. Universal biohazard warning signs posted at all entrances.
citation: Restricted lab access; biohazard warning signs.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: How should infectious waste generated in BSL-2 be segregated and ultimately treated?
back:
1. Segregate into Yellow Bags
2. Treat via on-site autoclave or high-temperature incineration (>1100°C).
citation: autoclave available for waste... Infectious & Anatomical Waste... Yellow Bag... Treated by High-Temperature Incineration.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: Differentiate BSL-2 from BSL-3 based on airflow and primary mode of infection.
back: BSL-2 handles ingestion/percutaneous risks with standard ventilation; BSL-3 requires negative air pressure and HEPA-filtered exhaust for inhalation hazards.
citation: BSL-2... Transmission via ingestion... BSL-3... inhalation/aerosol route... Controlled negative air pressure.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: Why must BSL-2 personnel wait 30 minutes before re-entering a room after an aerosol spill?
back: This delay allows suspended biological aerosols to settle, reducing the risk of inhalation exposure during cleanup.
citation: If an aerosol is generated, evacuate the room immediately and wait 30 minutes for aerosols to settle before re-entering.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 2
front: Q: Name two common enteric bacterial pathogens listed as BSL-2/Risk Group 2 agents.
back:
1. Salmonella spp.
2. Vibrio cholerae.
citation: Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella spp., Hepatitis B & C viruses, HIV, Vibrio cholerae.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: What defines Risk Group 4 (RG-4) agents handled in BSL-4 laboratories?
back:
- Dangerous and exotic agents
- High individual and community risk
- Aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections
- Lack of available vaccines or treatments
citation: BSL-4 | RG-4: Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk of aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections with no vaccines/treatments.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Describe the essential facility structural features for a BSL-4 laboratory.
back:
- Isolated building or zone
- Dedicated air supply
- Double-HEPA exhaust air filtration
- Full chemical decontamination shower exit
citation: BSL-4 | Isolated building/zone; positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC; dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust; full chemical decontamination shower exit.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Contrast the personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements of BSL-3 versus BSL-4.
back:
- BSL-3: N95 respirator, gown, and gloves.
- BSL-4: Positive-pressure, air-fed suits OR Class III glove-box Biosafety Cabinet (BSC).
citation: BSL-3 | BSC Class II or III; BSL-4 | positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: A lab receives a sample suspected of containing Ebola. Which Biosafety Level is mandatory?
back: BSL-4. It is required for high-risk, aerosol-transmissible, life-threatening agents like Ebola that lack standard vaccines or treatments.
citation: BSL-4 | Bio-Risk Organisms: Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: What is the mandatory exit protocol for personnel in a BSL-4 suit laboratory?
back: Personnel must pass through a full chemical decontamination shower to neutralize pathogens on the exterior of the positive-pressure suit before doffing.
citation: BSL-4 | full chemical decontamination shower exit.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: List four viral pathogens requiring BSL-4 containment according to WHO guidelines.
back:
1. Ebola virus
2. Marburg virus
3. Lassa virus
4. Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus
citation: BSL-4 | Bio-Risk Organisms: Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: How is primary containment achieved in BSL-4 without using positive-pressure suits?
back: Work is performed within a Class III Biosafety Cabinet (glove-box), providing a physical barrier via a sealed, gas-tight environment.
citation: BSL-4 | positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Why is Mycobacterium tuberculosis BSL-3 while Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever is BSL-4?
back: BSL-3 agents (M. tuberculosis) have available treatments/vaccines. BSL-4 agents (CCHF) are life-threatening with no available vaccines or medical countermeasures.
citation: BSL-3 | agents that may cause serious or potentially lethal disease... BSL-4 | life-threatening infections with no vaccines/treatments.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Describe the specific exhaust air requirements for a BSL-4 facility.
back: The facility must utilize a dedicated air supply and double-HEPA filtration for all exhaust air to prevent environmental release.
citation: BSL-4 | dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: What are the two configurations for BSL-4 laboratory operations?
back:
1. Suit Laboratory: Personnel in positive-pressure air-fed suits.
2. Cabinet Laboratory: Work handled in a Class III glove-box Biosafety Cabinet.
citation: BSL-4 | positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: Define Biosafety Level 1 (BSL-1) and the type of agents handled.
back: BSL-1 involves well-characterized agents (Risk Group 1) that do not consistently cause disease in healthy, immunocompetent humans.
citation: BSL-1: RG-1: Well-characterized agents not known to consistently cause disease in immunocompetent adult humans.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: Why is BSL-1 considered the lowest level of biocontainment?
back: It handles non-pathogenic organisms like E. coli K-12 which lack virulent mechanisms to cause systemic human disease.
citation: BSL-1: Well-characterized agents not known to consistently cause disease in immunocompetent adult humans.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: Contrast BSL-1 and BSL-2 regarding physical containment and benchwork.
back: BSL-1 allows open benchwork without mandatory Biosafety Cabinets; BSL-2 requires BSCs for aerosol-generating procedures and restricted access.
citation: BSL-1: open benchwork; ... BSL-2: Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) used for aerosol-generating procedures.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: A lab tech handles Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Identify the BSL level and essential hygiene facility.
back: BSL-1. The facility must have a dedicated handwashing sink for standard microbiological hygiene.
citation: BSL-1: Saccharomyces cerevisiae ... handwashing sink.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: What is the mandatory daily protocol for BSL-1 work surfaces?
back: Surfaces must be decontaminated daily and immediately after any spill of viable biological material.
citation: BSL-1: decontamination of work surfaces daily.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: List the fundamental Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) used in BSL-1.
back: 1. Lab coat; 2. Gloves (as needed); 3. Eye protection (standard safety protocol).
citation: BSL-1: personal protective equipment (lab coat, gloves as needed).

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: Which 'standard microbiological practice' is core to BSL-1 to prevent ingestion exposure?
back: Frequent handwashing and the strict prohibition of eating, drinking, or applying cosmetics in the lab.
citation: BSL-1: Standard microbiological practices; ... handwashing sink.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: Distinguish the containment requirements for E. coli K-12 vs. Staphylococcus aureus.
back: E. coli K-12 (BSL-1): Open benchwork. S. aureus (BSL-2): Restricted access and mandatory BSC for aerosols.
citation: BSL-1: E. coli (K-12 strains) ... BSL-2: Staphylococcus aureus.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: How does 'Mitigation' in the AMP model apply specifically to BSL-1?
back: Using low-level controls like standard SOPs, handwashing, and basic PPE to manage minimal biological risks.
citation: Mitigation: Implementing controls to reduce risk (e.g., ... facility design, vaccination, PPE, SOPs).

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 1
front: Name three representative micro-organisms handled under BSL-1 protocols.
back: 1. E. coli (K-12 strains); 2. Bacillus subtilis; 3. Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast).
citation: BSL-1: E. coli (K-12 strains), Bacillus subtilis, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, microflora.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Which specific bio-risk organisms (RG-4) require BSL-4 containment?
back:
1. Ebola virus
2. Marburg virus
3. Lassa virus
4. Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus
citation: BSL-4: Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: What primary containment equipment is unique to BSL-4 laboratory personnel?
back:
1. Positive-pressure air-fed suits
2. Class III glove-box Biosafety Cabinets (BSC)
citation: BSL-4: Positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Contrast the air exhaust requirements between BSL-3 and BSL-4 facilities.
back:
1. BSL-3: HEPA filtration of exhaust air.
2. BSL-4: Double-HEPA exhaust with a dedicated air supply.
citation: BSL-3: HEPA filtration of exhaust air... BSL-4: Dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Describe the mandatory exit procedure for personnel in a BSL-4 suit laboratory.
back:
1. Passage through a chemical decontamination shower
2. Mandatory isolation from public zones
3. Strict suit-doffing protocols
citation: BSL-4: Full chemical decontamination shower exit; Isolated building/zone.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Why is CCHF classified as a BSL-4 agent rather than BSL-3?
back:
1. High individual and community risk
2. Aerosol-transmitted
3. Life-threatening with no available vaccines/treatments
citation: BSL-4: Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk... with no vaccines/treatments.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: What are the two structural options for housing a BSL-4 facility?
back:
1. A completely isolated building
2. A strictly dedicated, sealed zone within a building
citation: BSL-4: Isolated building/zone.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: How is directional airflow maintained in BSL-4 compared to BSL-3?
back:
1. BSL-3: Controlled negative air pressure.
2. BSL-4: Dedicated air supply with double-HEPA filtration to ensure absolute containment of exotic aerosols.
citation: BSL-3: Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab)... BSL-4: Dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Which feature of BSL-4 prevents the community-wide spread of infectious aerosols?
back:
1. Double-HEPA filtration of exhaust
2. Sealed building construction
3. Chemical shower decontamination of outgoing personnel
citation: BSL-4: Dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust; full chemical decontamination shower exit.

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: What is the formal definition of Biological Waste?
back:
Waste generated during biological diagnosis, research, or treatment containing: 
- Viable microorganisms/cultured material
- Human tissues, blood, or body fluids
- Components capable of causing infection.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Biological Waste: Any waste generated during biological diagnosis, research, immunization, or treatment containing viable microorganisms, cultured material, human tissues, blood, or body fluids capable of causing infection.]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: What are the two mandatory treatment steps for contaminated recyclable plastics (Red Bag)?
back:
1. Autoclaving or Microwaving (Inactivation)
2. Shredding followed by recycling.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Red Bag: Segregated immediately. Treated by Autoclaving or Microwaving followed by shredding and recycling.]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: Differentiate between Yellow and Red bag waste contents.
back:
- Yellow Bag: Infectious/Anatomical waste (tissues, placentas, soiled dressings).
- Red Bag: Contaminated recyclable plastics (IV bottles, tubing, catheters).
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Yellow Bag: Human tissues, organs, body parts, placentas... Red Bag: Tubing, IV bottles, catheters, urine bags...]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: A doctor suffers a needle-stick injury. What are the two immediate first-aid steps?

1. Wash site immediately with soap and water.
2. Do NOT squeeze or suck the wound.
citation: Page 4 (Book Page): [Immediate Care: Wash needle-stick site immediately with soap and water. Do NOT squeeze or suck the wound.]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: Which specific chemical agent is used for disinfecting glassware waste (Blue Box)?

citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Blue Box / Bin: Disinfected with Sodium Hypochlorite / Autoclaving, then sent for glass recycling.]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: What is the maximum permissible storage duration for biological waste?
back: 24 to 48 hours in a dedicated, locked, and ventilated room.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Biological waste must be stored in a dedicated, locked, ventilated room marked with a biohazard symbol for a maximum of 24 to 48 hours.]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: How should a human placenta be disposed of according to UHS standards?

- Segregated into a Yellow Bag.
- Treated by High-Temperature Incineration (>1100°C) or deep burial.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Infectious & Anatomical Waste (placentas): Yellow Bag. Treated by High-Temperature Incineration (>1100°C) or deep burial.]

category: Define biological waste

citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Sharps Waste (broken contaminated glass): White Container. Contaminated Recyclable Plastics (IV bottles): Red Bag.]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: What specific temperature is required for the incineration of infectious anatomical waste?
back: Greater than 1100 degrees Celsius (>1100°C).
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Treated by High-Temperature Incineration (>1100°C) or deep burial.]

category: Define biological waste
