citation: Section 5: [Primary Receptacle] (Leak-proof + Absorbent) ---> [Secondary Packaging] (Leak-proof & Durable).

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: A technician is transporting CSF and Blood Cultures. What is the specific SOP regarding refrigeration?
back: Do NOT refrigerate CSF or blood cultures (unlike most specimens kept at 2–8°C).
citation: Section 6: Rapid transport at correct temperatures (2--8°C; do not refrigerate CSF or blood cultures).

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: Which specific label and symbol must be displayed on the rigid outer box during transport?
back:
1. UN 3373 Diamond Label.
2. Biohazard symbol.
citation: Section 5: Outer Packaging: A rigid outer box bearing the UN 3373 Diamond Label, Biohazard symbol.

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: What is the primary function of absorbent material within the Triple Packaging System?
back: To absorb the entire liquid contents of the primary receptacle in case of breakage.
citation: Section 5: wrapped in sufficient absorbent material (cotton, paper towels) to absorb the entire liquid contents if broken.

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: What identification and emergency information must be printed on the outer packaging?
back: Sender/recipient contact information and 24/7 emergency contact details.
citation: Section 5: Outer Packaging: A rigid outer box bearing... sender/recipient contact information, and 24/7 emergency contact details.

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: Differentiate the disposal of broken transport glassware versus liquid-soaked cleaning materials.
back: Broken glass: White puncture-proof container. Soaked materials: Yellow biohazard bag.
citation: Section 3: Dispose: Place spent cleaning material into a Yellow biohazard bag and broken glass into a White puncture-proof container.

category: Discuss the steps for the management of a laboratory spill
front: What is the first immediate action and required waiting time if a bio-spill generates aerosols?
back:
1. Notify lab personnel and evacuate immediately.
2. Wait 30 minutes for aerosols to settle before re-entering the area.
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [1. Evacuate & Alert: Notify lab personnel immediately. If an aerosol is generated, evacuate the room immediately and wait 30 minutes for aerosols to settle before re-entering.]

category: Discuss the steps for the management of a laboratory spill
front: Why is a 20-30 minute contact time mandatory after applying disinfectant to a biological spill?
back: This duration is required for complete microbial inactivation, ensuring the disinfectant effectively neutralizes all pathogens within the spill material.
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [5. Observe Contact Time: Allow an undisturbed contact time of 20 to 30 minutes for microbial inactivation.]

category: Discuss the steps for the management of a laboratory spill
front: Contrast the disposal containers used for spent absorbent towels versus contaminated broken glass during spill cleanup.
back:
1. Spent absorbent towels: Yellow biohazard bag.
2. Broken glass: White puncture-proof container.
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [7. Dispose: Place spent cleaning material into a Yellow biohazard bag and broken glass into a White puncture-proof container.]

category: Discuss the steps for the management of a laboratory spill
front: A technician spills a TB culture, creating aerosols. Outline the necessary PPE for re-entry and cleanup.
back:
1. Gown and heavy-duty utility gloves.
2. Eye protection (goggles/face shield).
3. Fitted N95 respirator.
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [2. Don PPE: Wear protective attire including a gown, heavy-duty utility gloves, eye protection (goggles/face shield), and an N95 respirator.]

category: Discuss the steps for the management of a laboratory spill
front: Identify the standard disinfectant and concentration used for neutralizing laboratory biological spills.
back: Freshly prepared 10% Sodium Hypochlorite (household bleach) solution.
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [4. Apply Disinfectant: Pour a freshly prepared disinfectant (10% Sodium Hypochlorite / household bleach solution) over the absorbent towels...]

category: Discuss the steps for the management of a laboratory spill
front: What specific directional technique must be used when covering a spill and applying disinfectant?
back: Work from the perimeter/outer edges inward to prevent the liquid and contamination from spreading further.
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [3. Cover the Spill: Gently place absorbent paper towels over the spill from the perimeter working inward to prevent liquid spread.]

category: Discuss the steps for the management of a laboratory spill
front: Describe the safe mechanical procedure for picking up soaked towels and glass after the contact time.
back: Use forceps, tongs, or a dustpan. Never use hands directly to handle contaminated materials or glass.
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [6. Mechanical Clean-up: Pick up soaked paper towels and broken glass using forceps, tongs, or a dustpan—never use hands directly.]

category: Discuss the steps for the management of a laboratory spill
front: Summarize the final three steps of the laboratory spill management protocol after mechanical cleanup.
back:
1. Dispose of waste (Yellow bag/White container).
2. Re-wipe area with disinfectant.
3. Doff PPE and perform thorough hand hygiene.
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [7. Dispose: ... 8. Decontaminate & Wash: Wipe the area again with disinfectant, doff PPE, dispose of disposable PPE, and perform thorough hand hygiene.]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: Under Standard Precautions, when must a healthcare professional wear gloves?
back: Gloves are required whenever touching blood, body fluids, secretions, or non-intact skin.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [Standard Precautions (All Patients): Wear gloves when touching blood, body fluids, secretions, or non-intact skin]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: What PPE is necessary for pathogens spread by direct contact (e.g., MRSA, VRE)?
back: Gown and gloves are mandatory for Contact Precautions.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [Contact Precautions: Gown and gloves for pathogens spread by direct contact (Clostridioides difficile, MRSA, VRE)]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: Contrast the respiratory protection required for Droplet versus Airborne precautions.
back:
- Droplet: Surgical mask and eye protection.
- Airborne: Fitted N95/FFP2 respirator.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [Droplet Precautions: Surgical mask and eye protection... Airborne Precautions: Fitted N95 / FFP2 respirator]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: In a patient with suspected Mycobacterium tuberculosis, what PPE and room settings are required?
back:
- PPE: Fitted N95/FFP2 respirator, gown, gloves, and eye protection.
- Setting: Negative-pressure isolation room.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [Airborne Precautions: Fitted N95 / FFP2 respirator, gown, gloves, and eye protection inside negative-pressure isolation rooms (Mycobacterium tuberculosis)]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: When should a gown and face shield be added to standard glove use?
back: These should be added if splashing or spraying of blood/body fluids is anticipated.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [add a gown/face shield if splashing is anticipated]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: List the specific PPE required for managing a laboratory biological spill.
back:
- Gown
- Heavy-duty utility gloves
- Eye protection (goggles/face shield)
- N95 respirator
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [Don PPE: Wear protective attire including a gown, heavy-duty utility gloves, eye protection (goggles/face shield), and an N95 respirator]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: What PPE is indicated when working within 3–6 feet of a patient with Influenza?
back: Surgical mask and eye protection (Droplet Precautions).
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [Droplet Precautions: Surgical mask and eye protection within 3–6 feet of coughing patients (Influenza)]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: For BSL-4 agents like Ebola, what extreme PPE/facility measure is used?
back: Positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box Biosafety Cabinets.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [BSL-4: Positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: Describe the correct order for donning (putting on) PPE.
back:
1. Gown
2. Mask/Respirator
3. Goggles/Face Shield
4. Gloves (over gown cuffs)
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [Donning Order (Putting On): Gown → Mask/Respirator → Goggles/Face Shield → Gloves]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: What is the first item removed during the PPE doffing (taking off) sequence?
back: Gloves are the first item removed.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [Doffing Order (Taking Off): Gloves → Goggles/Face Shield → Gown → Mask/Respirator]

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: What is the mandatory standard system for transporting Category B infectious substances?
back: The **Triple Packaging System (UN 3373)**.
citation: Section 5: To transport Category B infectious substances safely, the Triple Packaging System is mandatory.

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: Why must the primary receptacle be wrapped in absorbent material during transport?
back: To **absorb the entire liquid contents** in case of breakage or leakage.
citation: Section 5: primary container... wrapped in sufficient absorbent material (cotton, paper towels) to absorb the entire liquid contents if broken.

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: Contrast the physical requirements of primary versus secondary transport packaging.
back: Both must be **leak-proof**, but the secondary packaging must also be **durable** to protect the primary receptacle.
citation: Section 5: 1. Primary Receptacle: A leak-proof, water-tight primary container... 2. Secondary Packaging: A leak-proof, durable secondary container.

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: List four mandatory markings for the outer rigid box of a biological sample.
back:
1. **UN 3373 Diamond Label**
2. **Biohazard symbol**
3. Sender/recipient contact info
4. 24/7 emergency contact details.
citation: Section 5: Outer Packaging: A rigid outer box bearing the UN 3373 Diamond Label, Biohazard symbol, sender/recipient contact information, and 24/7 emergency contact details.

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: What are the two specific specimen types that must NOT be refrigerated during transport?
back:
1. **Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF)**
2. **Blood cultures**.
citation: Section 6: Rapid transport at correct temperatures (2-8°C; do not refrigerate CSF or blood cultures).

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: Which specific diamond label is required for transporting Category B infectious substances?
back: The **UN 3373** Diamond Label.
citation: Section 5: Outer Packaging: A rigid outer box bearing the UN 3373 Diamond Label.

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: Describe the sequence of specimen handling from identification to rapid transport.
back:
1. Double patient ID
2. Leak-proof primary tube collection
3. Enclosure in absorbent secondary containers
4. Temperature-controlled transport.
citation: Section 6: Specimen Handling: Double patient identification -> Collection in leak-proof primary tubes -> Enclosure in absorbent secondary containers -> Rapid transport at correct temperatures.

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: Compare the transport temperature of a routine viral swab versus a CSF specimen.
back: Viral swabs are typically transported at **2–8°C**, whereas CSF **must not be refrigerated**.
citation: Section 6: Rapid transport at correct temperatures (2-8°C; do not refrigerate CSF or blood cultures).

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: Outline the three layers of the Triple Packaging System from inside to outside.
back:
1. **Primary Receptacle** (leak-proof + absorbent)
2. **Secondary Packaging** (leak-proof & durable)
3. **Outer Rigid Box** (UN 3373 markings).
citation: Section 5: [ Primary Receptacle ] ---> [ Secondary Packaging ] ---> [ Outer Rigid Box ]

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: What is the primary safety requirement for the innermost container of a biological sample?
back: It must be **leak-proof** and **water-tight**.
citation: Section 5: 1. Primary Receptacle: A leak-proof, water-tight primary container.

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: When are gloves mandatory under Standard Precautions for all patients?
back:
- Touching blood, body fluids, or secretions
- Touching non-intact skin or mucous membranes
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [Standard Precautions (All Patients): Wear gloves when touching blood, body fluids, secretions, or non-intact skin; add a gown/face shield if splashing is anticipated.]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: What PPE is required for pathogens spread via direct contact like MRSA or VRE?
back:
- Gown
- Gloves
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [Contact Precautions: Gown and gloves for pathogens spread by direct contact (Clostridioides difficile, MRSA, VRE).]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: Distinguish PPE for Droplet vs. Airborne precautions regarding facial protection.
back:
- Droplet: Surgical mask and eye protection (within 3-6 feet).
- Airborne: Fitted N95 / FFP2 respirator.
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [Droplet Precautions: Surgical mask and eye protection... Airborne Precautions: Fitted N95 / FFP2 respirator...]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: Which PPE must be donned when managing a biological lab spill after 30 minutes?
back:
- Gown
- Heavy-duty utility gloves
- Goggles/face shield
- N95 respirator
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [Don PPE: Wear protective attire including a gown, heavy-duty utility gloves, eye protection (goggles/face shield), and an N95 respirator.]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: What is the mandatory sequence for doffing (removing) PPE to prevent self-contamination?
back:
1. Gloves
2. Goggles/Face Shield
3. Gown
4. Mask/Respirator (removed outside room)
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [Doffing Order (Taking Off): Gloves → Goggles/Face Shield → Gown → Mask/Respirator (removed outside room).]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: List the specific clinical conditions requiring full Airborne Precautions PPE.
back:
- Mycobacterium tuberculosis
- Measles
- Varicella
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [Airborne Precautions: Fitted N95 / FFP2 respirator, gown, gloves, and eye protection... (Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Measles, Varicella).]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: When should a healthcare worker add a gown and face shield to standard precautions?
back: - When splashing of blood, body fluids, or secretions is anticipated.
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [add a gown/face shield if splashing is anticipated.]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: A surgeon encounters surgical smoke plumes; what specific hazard and protection are relevant?
back:
- Hazard: Aerosolized viral particles (e.g., HPV).
- Protection: N95/FFP2 respirator (Airborne level).
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [Surgical Environments: ...surgical smoke plume hazards (aerosolized viral particles like HPV).]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: What is the correct sequence for donning (putting on) PPE before patient contact?
back:
1. Gown
2. Mask/Respirator
3. Goggles/Face Shield
4. Gloves (pulled over gown cuffs)
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [Donning Order (Putting On): Gown → Mask/Respirator → Goggles/Face Shield → Gloves (pulled over gown cuffs).]

category: Discuss the situations under which PPE should be used by the health care professionals
front: Q: Define the primary purpose of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).
back: Specialized attire protecting skin, mucous membranes, airways, and clothing from infectious agent contact.
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [Define Personal Protective Equipment: Specialized attire or equipment worn by healthcare personnel to protect skin, mucous membranes, airways, and clothing from contact with infectious agents.]

category: Define bio risk management
front: Q: What is the definition of Bio-risk Management (BRM)?
back: A system integrating hazard identification, risk assessment, mitigation measures, and performance evaluation to maintain biological risks at acceptable levels.
citation: Page 4 (Book Page): [Bio-risk Management is] a system that integrates hazard identification, risk assessment, mitigation measures, and performance evaluation to keep biological risks at acceptable levels.

category: Define bio risk management
front: Q: Describe the three pillars of the AMP model in Bio-risk Management.
back: 1. Assessment (identify hazards/consequences). 2. Mitigation (PPE, BSCs, SOPs). 3. Performance (audits and monitoring).
citation: Page 4 (Book Page): Assessment: Identifying hazards... Mitigation: Implementing controls... Performance: Auditing protocols, monitoring waste handling.

category: Define bio risk management
front: Q: Contrast the ventilation requirements for BSL-2 and BSL-3 laboratories.
back: BSL-2 uses standard ventilation with Biosafety Cabinets for aerosols; BSL-3 requires controlled negative air pressure and HEPA-filtered exhaust.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): BSL-2: Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) used for aerosol-generating procedures. BSL-3: Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); HEPA filtration of exhaust air.

category: Define bio risk management
front: Q: A biological spill generates aerosols. What is the immediate protocol before decontamination?
back: Immediately evacuate the room, notify personnel, and wait exactly 30 minutes for aerosols to settle before re-entering.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): 1. Evacuate & Alert: Notify lab personnel immediately. If an aerosol is generated, evacuate the room immediately and wait 30 minutes for aerosols to settle before re-entering.

category: Define bio risk management
front: Q: What is the pharmacological regimen and timing for HIV Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP)?
back: 3-drug antiretroviral therapy (ART) for 28 days, initiated ideally within 2 to 72 hours of exposure.
citation: Page 5 (Book Page): HIV PEP: Start 3-drug antiretroviral therapy (ART) within 2 to 72 hours for 28 days.

category: Define bio risk management
front: Q: Define biological waste according to healthcare safety standards.
back: Waste from diagnosis, research, or treatment containing microorganisms, tissues, or fluids capable of causing infection.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): Any waste generated during biological diagnosis, research, immunization, or treatment containing viable microorganisms, cultured material, human tissues, blood, or body fluids capable of causing infection.

category: Define bio risk management
front: Q: How are contaminated sharps and recyclable plastics segregated and treated?
back: Sharps: White puncture-proof container; autoclaved. Recyclable Plastics: Red bag; autoclaved or microwaved, then shredded/recycled.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): Red Bag: Contaminated Recyclable Plastics... Treated by Autoclaving or Microwaving. White Container: Sharps Waste... Treated by Autoclaving / Dry Heat.

category: Define bio risk management
front: Q: Differentiate the primary risk groups (RG) handled in BSL-3 versus BSL-4 labs.
back: BSL-3 (RG-3): Serious/lethal inhalation risk (e.g., Anthrax). BSL-4 (RG-4): Life-threatening aerosol risk, no vaccine/treatment (e.g., Ebola).
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): BSL-3: RG-3: agents that may cause serious or potentially lethal disease through inhalation... BSL-4: RG-4: Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk... with no vaccines/treatments.

category: Define bio risk management
front: Q: Outline the triple packaging system for transporting Category B infectious substances.
back: 1. Leak-proof Primary Receptacle with absorbent. 2. Leak-proof Secondary Packaging. 3. Rigid Outer Box with UN 3373 marking.
citation: Page 3 (Book Page): [Primary Receptacle] (Leak-proof + Absorbent) ---> [Secondary Packaging] (Leak-proof & Durable) ---> [Outer Rigid Box] (UN 3373 + Markings).

category: Define bio risk management
front: Q: What is the mandated sequence for doffing (removing) PPE?
back: Gloves → Goggles/Face Shield → Gown → Mask/Respirator (removed outside the room), followed by immediate hand hygiene.
citation: Page 3 (Book Page): Doffing Order (Taking Off): Gloves -> Goggles/Face Shield -> Gown -> Mask/Respirator (removed outside room).

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: What are the two mandatory physical properties of the Primary Receptacle in triple packaging?
back:
1. Leak-proof.
2. Water-tight (e.g., blood collection tube).
citation: Section 5: Primary Receptacle: A leak-proof, water-tight primary container (e.g., blood collection tube).

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: Describe the specific mechanical role of the Secondary Packaging in biological transport.
back: It acts as a leak-proof, durable container that encloses and protects the primary receptacle(s).
citation: Section 5: Secondary Packaging: A leak-proof, durable secondary container that encloses and protects the primary receptacle(s).

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: Distinguish the Primary layer from the Secondary layer regarding absorbent material placement.
back: Absorbent material (cotton/paper) is placed around the Primary Receptacle, inside the Secondary Packaging, to soak up potential leaks.
citation: Section 5: Primary Receptacle... wrapped in sufficient absorbent material (cotton, paper towels) to absorb the entire liquid contents if broken.

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: A technician is transporting CSF and Blood cultures. What temperature error must be avoided?
back: Do NOT refrigerate. These must be transported at room temperature, unlike most samples which require 2-8°C.
citation: Section 6: Rapid transport at correct temperatures (2–8°C; do not refrigerate CSF or blood cultures).

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: What is the specific volume capacity requirement for absorbent material used in triple packaging?
back: It must be sufficient to absorb the entire liquid volume of the primary receptacle in case of breakage.
citation: Section 5: wrapped in sufficient absorbent material (cotton, paper towels) to absorb the entire liquid contents if broken.

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: List the four mandatory markings/labels required on the Outer Rigid Box for biological samples.
back:
1. UN 3373 Diamond Label.
2. Biohazard symbol.
3. Sender/Recipient contact info.
4. 24/7 Emergency contact.
citation: Section 5: Outer Packaging: A rigid outer box bearing the UN 3373 Diamond Label, Biohazard symbol, sender/recipient contact information, and 24/7 emergency contact details.

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: How is the Triple Packaging System (UN 3373) conceptually organized from innermost to outermost layer?
back: Primary Receptacle (Leak-proof) -> Secondary Packaging (Durable) -> Outer Packaging (Rigid Box).
citation: Section 5: [ Primary Receptacle ] ---> [ Secondary Packaging ] ---> [ Outer Rigid Box ]

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: During transit, a primary tube of Category B substance leaks. Which two layers prevent environmental contamination?
back:
1. The Absorbent Material (soaks the liquid).
2. The Leak-proof Secondary Packaging (contains the fluid).
citation: Section 5: Secondary Packaging: A leak-proof, durable secondary container that encloses and protects... Primary Receptacle... wrapped in sufficient absorbent material.

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: What is the standard temperature range for the rapid transport of most infectious specimens?
back: 2°C to 8°C (excluding CSF and blood cultures).
citation: Section 6: Rapid transport at correct temperatures (2–8°C; do not refrigerate CSF or blood cultures).

category: Discuss the SOP of transportation of biological samples
front: Q: Which specific UN code is designated for the transportation of Category B infectious substances?
citation: Section 5: Outer Packaging: A rigid outer box bearing the UN 3373 Diamond Label.
